core_principles.text: To maximize muscle hypertrophy, individuals should employ a range of motion that emphasizes training at long muscle lengths.
To maximize muscle hypertrophy, individuals should employ a repetition tempo between 2 and 8 seconds.

specific_findings.text: A narrative review recommends employing a repetition tempo between 2 and 8 seconds to maximize muscle hypertrophy.

core_principles.text: Both eccentric and concentric actions should be employed in order to maximize muscle hypertrophy.
A combination of slower eccentric and faster concentric repetition seems to be best for maximizing muscular development.
A repetition duration of approximately 3 to 8 seconds per repetition is suggested to support muscular development.

common_mistakes.text: Performing repetitions in a 'super slow' manner may have a detrimental effect on muscle hypertrophy.

specific_findings.text: A systematic review and meta-analysis by Schoenfeld et al. found that a wide range of repetition durations (0.5 to 8 s) resulted in similar hypertrophy.
Wilk et al. suggested a repetition duration of ~3 to ~8 s per repetition based on a review of tempo influence on hypertrophy and strength.

Keeler et al. found that when the duration of the eccentric phase was similar among conditions (5 vs. 4 s), prolonging the duration of the concentric phase (10 s) did not increase lean body mass when compared to a faster concentric phase (2 s).

core_principles.text: Eccentric actions should be performed in a sufficiently controlled manner to ensure that the muscle controls the descent of the weight rather than relying solely on gravitational forces.

common_mistakes.text: Relying solely on gravitational forces to lower the weight during the eccentric phase instead of controlling the descent with the target muscle.

specific_findings.text: Nogueira et al. [16] demonstrated that a faster concentric phase duration of 1 second resulted in significantly greater biceps brachii hypertrophy when compared to a slower concentric phase duration of 3 seconds in a cohort of older men.

Pereira et al. [17] found that performing a 4-second eccentric phase elicited greater absolute biceps brachii hypertrophy when compared to a 1-second eccentric phase, with both groups employing a 1-second concentric repetition tempo.
A systematic review by Kassiano et al. [26] found that a partial range of motion at long muscle lengths is sufficient to promote optimal muscle growth for the biceps brachii.

core_principles.text: Strict technique on a barbell biceps curl involves maintaining a more upright posture with minimal hip and leg drive to direct maximum stimulation to the target muscle group.

common_mistakes.text: Non-strict technique on a barbell biceps curl involves using a variable posture that sways back and forth, which permits assistance from the gluteals, erector spinae, and other ancillary muscles.

consequences.text: Using excessive amounts of momentum during an exercise results in lower loading of the target muscles, which can potentially impair the hypertrophic stimulus.

core_principles.text: Employ a range of motion that allows the target muscle to be fully stretched.
Utilize an eccentric and concentric phase duration that spans an overall repetition duration of 2 to 8 seconds.
Diminish the involvement of non-target muscles by minimizing the use of external momentum when possible.

common_mistakes.text: Involving unintended muscle groups, such as the hip extensors, to generate movement during a bicep curl.
Performing partial repetitions at shorter muscle lengths rather than allowing the muscle to fully stretch.

specific_findings.text: A repetition tempo of 2–8 s seems to be sufficient to maximize hypertrophy.
Partial repetitions at shorter-muscle lengths are not as hypertrophic as partial repetitions at longer-muscle lengths.

consequences.text: Involving non-target muscles that work primarily at short muscle lengths (such as the hip extensors during a bicep curl) generates fatigue that may not be worth the trade-off, as they are unlikely to benefit from the stimulus.

core_principles.text: It is recommended to minimize the involvement of other joints to ensure repetitions adhere to the recommended repetition tempo and range of motion.
To maximize muscle growth, the repetition technique should emphasize training at long muscle lengths within the range of motion.
Eccentric and concentric repetition tempos can vary based on preference, as long as the total repetition length is between 2 and 8 seconds.

specific_findings.text: Based on current literature, total repetition length (including eccentric and concentric phases) should be between 2 and 8 s to maximize hypertrophy.
